title: The distribution-memory waste's bounded trait cloud does not depend on the random-feature draw: other frequencies give the same plateau (seed 6, T=6000)
summary: Replicate of 20261028T0700-c63-vortex-distribution-memory on seed 6 / mut_seed 6 (standard waste) with rff_seed 1 instead of 0, so the kernel's anisotropy and tail revivals are drawn independently. Cloud radius per 1000 t: 0.31, 0.58, 0.56, 0.56, 0.55, 0.56 (rff_seed 0: 0.32, 0.53, 0.61, 0.64, 0.59, 0.59; mean-trait waste 0.23 -> 0.84); hull 1.32 (rff_seed 0: 1.39; mean waste 2.10); share on new ground 0.03, 0.09, 0.00, 0.01 (rff_seed 0: 0.08, 0.04, 0.01, 0.02). So the early plateau at R ~0.55-0.6 and the end of new ground by t~5000 are properties of a waste that remembers the trait distribution at this lifetime, not of one kernel draw.

finding.operator: kind-specific waste that stores the eaters' trait distribution (random features), second frequency draw
finding.control: same seed and mutation draws, rff_seed 0 vs 1, and c61's mean-waste arm
finding.result: R at t=6000 0.56 (rff_seed 1), 0.59 (rff_seed 0), 0.84 (mean waste); hull 1.32, 1.39, 2.10; new ground after t=5000 <= 0.02 in both rff arms
